paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: the LORD does not leave His people in the ditch. Jerusalem drained the cup of His fury to the dregs, and the prophet says that among all her sons there was no one to take her hand (Isaiah 51:17-18). Then the LORD, who defends His people, says, "See, I have removed from your hand the cup of staggering." and promises she will never drink from it again (Isaiah 51:22). That's the God we serve, and He does the lifting Himself.

Now look at how the LORD frees her. He says, "You were sold for nothing, and without money you will be redeemed" (Isaiah 52:3). Friend, I went for 25 cents at a closing sale, and even I know you can't buy your way out of a hole like that. So the LORD calls her to wake up, shake off her dust and put on her garments of splendor (Isaiah 52:1-2), and He tells those who carry His vessels, "Depart, depart, go out from there!" and to purify themselves (Isaiah 52:11).

And the news is so good that somebody has to run and tell it: "How beautiful on the mountains are the feet of those who bring good news, who proclaim peace, who bring good tidings, who proclaim salvation, who say to Zion, “Your God reigns!”" (Isaiah 52:7). He doesn't send His people out the door in a panic, either, because "the LORD goes before you, and the God of Israel is your rear guard" (Isaiah 52:12). He's out in front and He's right behind them, and that's a God worth trusting, friend. So keep that oven warm.
